title: Minimum Number of Swaps to Make the String Balanced
summary: Given a string s of even length n, containing exactly n/2 opening and n/2 closing brackets, determine the minimum number of swaps needed to make the string balanced.
statement: Given a string s of even length n, containing exactly n/2 opening and n/2 closing brackets, determine the minimum number of swaps needed to make the string balanced. A string is balanced if it can be written as the empty string, a concatenation of two balanced strings, or a pair of brackets enclosing a balanced string.
constraints: s has even length 2 through 1000000 and contains only '[' and ']'.
The counts of opening and closing brackets are equal.
One operation may swap any two positions; return the minimum swaps needed for a balanced bracket string.
reference_solution:
def minimum_bracket_balance_swaps(s):
    balance = 0
    deficit = 0
    for char in s:
        balance += 1 if char == "[" else -1
        deficit = max(deficit, -balance)
    return (deficit + 1) // 2

        deficit += balance < 0

hints: The most negative prefix balance measures the maximum number of unmatched closing brackets seen at once.
One arbitrary swap brings an opening bracket forward and can repair two units of maximum deficit, so round half the deficit upward.
Scan balance (+1 for [, -1 for ]), retain deficit=max(deficit,-balance), return (deficit+1)//2.
Each swap changes the affected prefix balance by two, giving the lower bound; swapping an early unmatched close with a later open repeatedly attains that bound.

tests.explanation: One swap can transform the string into a balanced arrangement.
The deepest prefix deficit is three, so two arbitrary-position swaps are necessary and sufficient.
